goal: Prove GET /api/chat actually works end to end with a live call through the real AppHost, and fix whatever real problem that live test surfaces.

steps.action: Start ProjectName.AppHost fresh (no locked processes) and confirm both projectname-runtime (5044) and projectname-orchestrationapi (5200) respond on their root endpoints.
Call GET /api/chat on OrchestrationApi (the full OrchestrationApi -> gRPC -> Runtime -> IChatClient -> Ollama path) and record the result.

If the call fails, diagnose root cause with real evidence rather than assuming; if it is the previously-known 30s resilience-handler timeout, verify whether the earlier per-client override actually took effect.
Fix the root cause if found, rebuild, restart the AppHost, and re-run the live /api/chat call plus Runtime's own /chat endpoint to confirm the fix holds across repeated calls.
Shut down the AppHost cleanly, verify git status is limited to the intended fix, and commit and push.

success_criteria: GET http://localhost:5200/api/chat returns HTTP 200 with a real Ollama-generated response, exercising the full OrchestrationApi -> gRPC -> Runtime -> Ollama path
The call succeeds repeatably (more than one call in the same run), not just once by timing luck
Any root cause found for a failure is fixed at its actual source, not worked around or deferred without evidence
dotnet build ProjectName.slnx succeeds with 0 errors after any fix
Fix committed and pushed to origin
out_of_scope: Wiring the Pmcro__RuntimeRoot/TrailRoot/QueueRoot/SkillsRoot env vars into either Program.cs -- noted in the original seed as a secondary consideration, left for its own task
The AppHost GPU/SIGSEGV comment -- already absent from AppHost.cs, confirmed in a prior cycle
Any change to pmcro-aspire or the marketplace manifests
name_rationale: Names exactly what this cycle does: a live, not code-review-only, verification of the gRPC gateway.
